title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 69-71): K is a number field and Γ = Gal(K̄/K). X is a K-scheme, typically an anabelian curve. Γ acts on the profinite fundamental groupoid Π̂1(X_K̄). Grothendieck restricts to the full subgroupoid on Γ-fixed (K-rational) base points. For such a point, u ∈ Γ sends a path l: x→y to another path ^u l: x→y. Two elements compare them, as in (8)/(9): g_l(u) = ^u l · l^{-1} ∈ π̂1(X,y) and f_l(u) = l^{-1} · ^u l ∈ π̂1(X,x).

Generators (this page). For a finite set I of rational points, the full subgroupoid Π̂1(X_K̄, I) has a finite generating system. Pick x0 ∈ I. For each x ∈ I∖{x0} pick a path l_x: x0→x. Add a finite set of topological generators l_i of π̂1(X_K̄, x0). Because of the cocycle rule below, the values g_{l_α}(u) on these generators determine g_l(u) for every path l in the subgroupoid.

Conjecture-like remark. 'Il se pourrait que', in fairly general conditions (e.g. X an anabelian algebraic curve), the action of u on Π̂1(X_K̄, I) determines u. In modern terms: the Galois representation Γ_K → Aut(Π̂1(X_K̄, I)), or its outer version, is injective.

Research question. How do the invariants g_{l_α}(u) for X allow one to recover the invariants g_l(u) for OTHER K-schemes Y? This is the germ of the idea that one 'basic' parametrisation (e.g. on P^1∖{0,1,∞} or M_{0,4}) controls the action on the whole tower of moduli spaces.

Same-scheme case. Multiplicativity of l ↦ ^u l gives formula (10). For x --l'--> y --l''--> z: g_u(l''l') = g_u(l'') · l''(g_u(l')), where l''(h) := l'' h l''^{-1} is transport of structure from π̂1(y) to π̂1(z). The next page gives the f-version (11), the n-fold composite (12), and (crossed out) the remark that l ↦ g_l is a 1-cocycle whose torsors are the Hom-sets Hom(x,y).
errors: No mathematical error in (10). Check: ^u(l''l') = ^u l''·^u l' = g(l'')l''·g(l')l' = g(l'')·(l''g(l')l''^{-1})·l''l'.
Notation slip: generators 'de π1(X,x0)' should be of the geometric group π̂1(X_K̄, x0). Likewise Π̂1(X_K, I) should read Π̂1(X_K̄, I) (the image shows a hat on Π; the bar on K is ambiguous).

Gap: the reduction to rational points is restrictive. Many anabelian curves have few or no K-rational points, and P^1∖{0,1,∞} has none in the open part. Later work (Deligne; Ihara; Grothendieck's own Esquisse) uses tangential base points instead.
The determination claim is stated only as a possibility ('il se pourrait'), not proved.

ideas.what: Encoding the Galois action on a groupoid with rational base points by the elements g_l(u) = ^u l·l^{-1} (resp. f_l(u) = l^{-1}·^u l), with a finite generating system (base point x0, connecting paths l_x, generators of π1(x0)).
ideas.modern_name: Galois cocycles on path torsors; Ihara's f_σ / Drinfeld–Ihara parametrisation σ ↦ (χ(σ), f_σ) via the path from 0⃗1 to 1⃗0
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme (1984), §2 on the Teichmüller tower and Γ-action; the explicit cocycle formulas themselves are not published

ideas.modern_name: Non-abelian 1-cocycle on the groupoid; path torsors Hom(x,y) as π1-torsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne; Deligne 1989 for path torsors)

ideas.what: Suggestion that for anabelian curves the action on Π̂1(X_K̄, I) determines u ∈ Γ (faithfulness).
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity of Γ_K → Out(π̂1(X_K̄)) for hyperbolic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Belyi (1979) for P^1∖{0,1,∞}; Matsumoto (1996) for affine hyperbolic curves; Hoshi–Mochizuki (2011) for general hyperbolic curves
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un Programme (faithfulness for P^1∖{0,1,∞} via Belyi); the general anabelian curve case is not stated there as far as I know

ideas.what: Question: how the Galois invariants g_{l_α}(u) on one scheme X determine the analogous invariants on other K-schemes Y.
ideas.modern_name: Reconstruction of the Γ-action on the Teichmüller tower from low levels; Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates, around 1978-81, the faithfulness of the Galois action on the profinite fundamental groupoid with rational base points for general anabelian curves, not just P^1∖{0,1,∞}. This anticipates Matsumoto (1996) and Hoshi–Mochizuki (2011). The question was later taken up and solved, so it is historical priority only, not an open thread.
missed.quote: Il se pourrait que dans des conditions assez générales (p. ex. si X est une courbe alg. anabélienne) la connaissance de l'opération u sur Π̂1(X_K, I) ... déterminer u
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents an early date for the general faithfulness question attributed to Grothendieck; relevant for historical credit rather than new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is careful bookkeeping of Galois cocycles on path groupoids; the g_l(u) are essentially Ihara's later f_σ. The faithfulness remark for general anabelian curves and the 'other schemes Y' question are early, private formulations of ideas later published (Esquisse) or proved by others. Mild historical interest, no new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'u_l' (twice) should read '^u l' (Galois conjugate of the path l), as on p. 69.
'choisir pour ∀ x ∈ I∖x0' — the symbol is Grothendieck's shorthand for 'tout'.

Lines 8-11: 'la connaissance de l'opération u sur Π̂1(X_K̄, I) (u ∈ Γ) [suffit à — struck through] déterminer u'. The insertion above reads roughly 'pour un ...' / 'pourrait'; '(u ∈ Γ)' is written below the line, not as part of the text.
'la formule donne en principe' — the formula referred to is (8)/(9) from p. 69.
Margin NB (rotated) reads approximately: 'NB pour la commodité, on ne regarde que les x ∈ X_K qui sont dans I, et le syst. choisi fini de générateurs (6)'. This is uncertain.
Equation (10): left side is g_{l''l'}(u) (overwritten in the manuscript); the second form is g_u(l''l') = g_u(l'')·l''(g_u(l')).
